label: Stop 2: The Grote Markt, with the town hall and the Brabo fountain

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And we've arrived. Wow. That's a lot of gold.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That's the Grote Markt, the Great Market.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The main square of the old city.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: It's a bit of a stage set.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In a good way. Turn around slowly.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: On one side, the town hall. On the other sides, tall narrow houses, with gilded statues on the roofs.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Those are guild houses.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Guild houses. So, clubs for craftsmen.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Associations for trades. Each one wanted a grand house on the best square.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It was a way of showing off.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So it's the original who-has-the-nicest-front-door contest.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Basically.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Now the big building. The town hall.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: When was that built?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It was inaugurated in 1565. It's a Renaissance building, designed by Cornelis Floris and Willem van den Broeck.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And it's still standing.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It is, but not without trouble.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And this is the part where we stop joking.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Understood.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In November 1576, Spanish troops sacked Antwerp.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's known as the Spanish Fury.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: About 6,000 people were killed and about 800 houses burned.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the town hall?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The courtyard of the town hall had been used as an arsenal, and the fire in the sack gutted the building.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It was rebuilt in its original style in the years that followed.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That's hard to imagine, standing here.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Most of what you see around you was either built before that, rebuilt after it, or both.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The city lost something that day it never fully got back.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And then it got worse.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A few years later, in 1585, a long siege ended with Alessandro Farnese, the Duke of Parma, taking the city for Spain.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Protestants were forced to leave.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Many of the skilled people and their money moved north, to Amsterdam.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And that's the end of the golden age.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's the beginning of the end.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Then in 1648 the river was closed.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: By 1800, fewer than 40,000 people lived here.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So the grand square we're standing in was built by a city at the top of its power.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And has outlived it. Now. Let's lighten things up a little.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Turn to the fountain in the middle.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. That's dramatic. A man on top, throwing something.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That's Brabo. The fountain was made by the sculptor Jef Lambeaux in 1887.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And Lambeaux lived in a house right on this square.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So the artist could look out the window at his own fountain.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: I'd have done the same. Now look at the figures.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A man at the top. And a giant at the bottom, lying on the rocks.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Without his head and without his hand.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And Brabo, up high, is just about to throw that hand into the river.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Oh, so it's the moment before the throw.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The moment of the throw. Look at the arm.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay, so that's my second hand.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: My tally says two. Even if one's on a statue.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: I'll allow it. Statues count.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the women?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Three nude women, around the base.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: They're holding symbols of Antwerp, a boat, and a fort, which is Het Steen, where we just were.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So it ties up the whole story.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Boat, fort, giant, hero.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's an advertisement for the town, in bronze.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Anything else to spot?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Look up at the guild house roofs.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The golden figures. Look at the town hall's front, the flags, and the central tower of the building.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And notice how much of it is a pedestrian zone.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You can wander the whole square.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And terraces. I can see cafés.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Plenty of them. A coffee here is a fair price for the view.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: There's also a famous old brown café on the square, Den Engel, at number 3, a historic place with a smoke-darkened ceiling and a mix of locals and visitors.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: If you want to sit for ten minutes, that's the sort of place.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Is that the champagne spot?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: No. Save that one. We'll point you at one near the end.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Good. I'm saving myself.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Pause here as long as you like.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Walk around the fountain. Take your photo.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Where next?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Look over the rooftops. You'll see a very tall tower.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That's the cathedral. Keep it in front of you, and take the short streets toward it.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You'll be at the church in about three minutes.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Just follow the tower.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Just follow the tower.
